title: Get ready to flee, Americans in ten countries warned as US embassies issue stark alert over spiraling Iran war
excerpt: The US Embassy has urgently advised US citizens across the Middle East to 'consider departing or be ready to depart if there is an escalation,' just hours after Trump signaled fresh strikes on Iran.
content_html:
Americans have been told to be 'ready' to flee ten Middle Eastern countries as the Iran war spirals, with President Trump warning: 'We'll be hitting them very hard.' 

The US Embassy has urgently advised US citizens across the Middle East to 'consider departing or be ready to depart if there is an escalation,' just hours after Trump signaled fresh strikes on Iran could come as soon as this weekend. 

The warning now covers 10 countries: the United Arab Emirates (UAE), Qatar, Oman, Iraq, Jordan, Israel, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Bahrain and, most recently, Egypt. 

'US Embassies across the Middle East have issued security alerts today advising travelers to exercise heightened vigilance and be prepared for flight cancellations and airspace closures,' the initial alert said.

Less than an hour later, a second alert announced that the warning had also been issued by the US Embassy in Cairo, Egypt.

For the first time, the warning told Americans in the region they should 'consider departing, or be prepared to depart should there be escalation,' bringing the guidance in line with other Middle Eastern countries.

'The situation in the Middle East remains fluid,' the alert read.

'The Iranian regime is unpredictable, as seen by its recent decisions to attack areas in the region without warning or provocations as well as to expand attacks to areas not previously targeted (such as Egypt).'

The US Embassy has urgently advised US citizens across ten Middle Eastern countries on Saturday morning to 'consider departing or be ready to depart if there is an escalation'

The alert comes hours after President Donald Trump signaled fresh strikes on Iran, warning: 'We'll be hitting them very hard'

The warning covers the United Arab Emirates (UAE), Qatar, Oman, Iraq , Jordan, Israel (pictured), Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Bahrain and, most recently, Egypt

It comes after sources told CBS News on Friday that the US and Israel are preparing what was described as 'one of the harshest bombing campaigns to date' against Iran's energy infrastructure. 

While the president has not yet given the final green light, several insiders told the outlet that strikes could begin as soon as this weekend, with Israel already notified and coordinating with Washington.

'The Department of War is locked and loaded, ready to execute the President's directives at a moment's notice,' Chief Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell said in a statement, though refused to comment on intended targets.

Meanwhile, an Israeli official told the outlet: 'Israel is unaware of any decision to restart full military operations, nor has Israel been asked to join any military action against Iran.'

A former US military official told CBS News that striking Iran's energy infrastructure would aim to cripple the regime's ability to support its military, provide services and maintain control. 

Trump signaled the threat of fresh strikes during a televised Cabinet meeting at Camp David on Friday, declaring: 'We will be hitting them very hard and, at some point, they're going to say, "We just can't take it anymore."'

Asked about the possibility of reviving diplomacy, the president told reporters: 'I think we just want to win.'

His comments come as the US demands Tehran reopen the Strait of Hormuz and honor a truce agreement that was forged last month but quickly fell apart. 

During a televised Cabinet meeting at Camp David on Friday, Trump signaled the threat of fresh strikes and said, 'at some point, they're going to say, "We just can't take it anymore"'

Sources told CBS News on Friday that the US and Israel are preparing what was described as 'one of the harshest bombing campaigns to date' against Iran's energy infrastructure

Trump's comments come as the US demands Tehran reopen the Strait of Hormuz and honor a truce agreement that was forged last month but quickly fell apart

After the Cabinet meeting, White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt accused Tehran of violating a truce memorandum of understanding with the US, claiming it 'broke it, shot at commercial ships and killed American soldiers.'

'President Trump is not going to stand by and allow this terrorist behavior to occur,' she said Friday evening. 'Iran will continue to pay until they come to the table in, what President Trump deems, a meaningful way.'

In a separate statement to CBS News, Leavitt said: 'As President Trump said at his cabinet meeting today, the United States will win, and Iran will not have a nuclear weapon under his watch.'

A joint operation would see Israel return to the battlefield after pausing its attacks under the US-brokered truce. Iran has not struck Israel since the agreement fell apart and Washington restarted combat operations in early July. 

A senior Iranian security official vowed Tehran has 'the capacity and the will' to retaliate against any US and Israeli strikes, claiming 'extensive response plans' are already prepared. 

The unnamed official told Iran's semi-official Tasnim News Agency that potential US-Israeli attacks would amount to a 'form of recklessness' on their part. 

The Iranian official claimed the 'comprehensive' plan includes strikes on 'the vital infrastructure of the Zionist regime and US energy infrastructure in the region.'

'We are fully prepared to carry it out,' the official added. 

A joint operation would see Israel return to the battlefield after pausing its attacks under the US-brokered truce

White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt told CBS News: 'As President Trump said at his cabinet meeting today, the United States will win, and Iran will not have a nuclear weapon under his watch'

An unnamed Iranian official claimed the territory's 'comprehensive' plan includes strikes on 'the vital infrastructure of the Zionist regime and US energy infrastructure in the region'

Early Saturday morning, Iran's military accused the US of 'escalating tensions' in the Middle East and warned countries in the region against cooperating with Washington. 

'The United States is rapidly moving down the path of escalating tensions in the region,' Ali Abdollahi, head of Iran's military central command, said.

In comments carried by Iran’s IRIB broadcaster, Abdollahi said regional countries should understand that the US intends to use their wealth, infrastructure and resources 'as a defensive shield for its weakened military.'

'Any country serving as defensive shield for criminal and aggressive America will be engulfed by the flames of war,' he added.

Iran launched drone attacks on Kuwait early Saturday, a Gulf nation that hosts US forces, and said it had struck oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz - the vital global energy route that has been largely shut down amid the fighting.

Kuwait's military said it 'intercepted and destroyed' hostile drones that entered its airspace, hours after it activated air defenses over what it called 'Iranian aggression.' No casualties were reported.

Meanwhile, in Gaza, Israeli strikes left a huge crater at a hospital less than 48 hours after President Trump said Hamas and Israel had agreed to advance a ceasefire plan in what he called a potential breakthrough in peace efforts. 

Trump announced Thursday that Hamas had agreed to 'completely disarm' in exchange for an Israeli troop withdrawal. But an Israeli official told CNN that Israel would not pull back its forces until Hamas was disarmed first. 

In Gaza, Israeli strikes left a huge crater at a hospital less than 48 hours after President Trump said Hamas and Israel had agreed to advance a ceasefire plan

Saturday's attack on the medical warehouse destroyed vital medical supplies, set dozens of nearby tents on fire and leveled a surrounding displacement camp

Last week, Trump vowed on Truth Social to bomb and destroy an Iranian bridge or power plant for every attack on a ship in the Strait of Hormuz

Israel then launched another round of strikes in Gaza on Saturday, destroying two medical warehouses at Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital and damaging two others, according to the territory’s health ministry. 

In recent months, Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital has become a crucial lifeline for displaced Palestinians and residents of central Gaza, serving as the only medical facility in the area capable of handling a large number of patients. 

'When medicines are bombed, illness becomes a weapon of war,' Dr Munir Al-Bursh, the ministry’s director general, said in a statement.

The attack, which came minutes after Israel’s army issued a forced displacement order, destroyed vital medical supplies, set dozens of nearby tents on fire and leveled a surrounding displacement camp. 

Footage showed people searching through the crater for medical supplies, including IV fluids, breathing tubes, surgical masks and cotton balls buried under the rubble.

'Destroying a medical warehouse while Gaza’s health system is already suffering from a 51 percent shortage of essential medicine is a direct assault on one of the last remaining lifelines of healthcare,' Dr Al-Bursh added.

The US has already struck bridges with both military and civilian uses during the conflict, a US official said, according to CBS.

Officials also weighed a potential move to cut electricity across Tehran on Friday, but stopped short of making a decision. 

Last week, Trump vowed on Truth Social to bomb and destroy an Iranian bridge or power plant for every attack on a ship in the Strait of Hormuz.

content_html_zh:
随着伊朗战争的升级，美国人被告知要“准备好”逃离十个中东国家，特朗普总统警告说：“我们将严厉打击他们。”

就在特朗普暗示最快本周末可能对伊朗发动新的打击几小时后，美国大使馆紧急建议中东地区的美国公民“考虑离开，或者在局势升级时准备离开”。

该警告现已覆盖 10 个国家：阿拉伯联合酋长国 (UAE)、卡塔尔、阿曼、伊拉克、约旦、以色列、科威特、沙特阿拉伯、巴林以及最近的埃及。

最初的警报称，“美国驻中东各国大使馆今天发布了安全警报，建议旅客提高警惕，并为航班取消和空域关闭做好准备。”

不到一个小时后，第二次警报宣布，美国驻埃及开罗大使馆也发出了这一警告。

该警告首次告诉该地区的美国人，他们应该“考虑离开，或者在局势升级时准备离开”，使该指导方针与其他中东国家保持一致。

警报中写道：“中东局势仍然不稳定。”

“伊朗政权难以预测，从其最近决定在没有警告或挑衅的情况下袭击该地区地区以及将袭击范围扩大到以前没有瞄准的地区（例如埃及）就可以看出这一点。”

美国大使馆周六上午紧急建议中东十个国家的美国公民“考虑离开，或者在局势升级时做好离开的准备”

就在特朗普总统发出对伊朗发动新一轮打击的几个小时后，警告称：“我们将严厉打击他们”

此前有消息人士周五告诉哥伦比亚广播公司新闻，美国和以色列正在准备对伊朗能源基础设施进行所谓的“迄今为止最严厉的轰炸行动之一”。

虽然总统尚未最终批准，但几位内部人士告诉媒体，袭击最早可能在本周末开始，以色列已经通知并与华盛顿协调。

五角大楼首席发言人肖恩·帕内尔(Sean Parnell)在一份声明中表示，“陆军部已经上膛，准备立即执行总统的指令”，但拒绝就预定目标发表评论。

与此同时，一名以色列官员告诉媒体：“以色列不知道任何重启全面军事行动的决定，也没有要求以色列加入任何针对伊朗的军事行动。”

一名前美国军方官员告诉哥伦比亚广播公司新闻，袭击伊朗的能源基础设施旨在削弱该政权支持其军事、提供服务和维持控制的能力。

当被问及恢复外交的可能性时，总统告诉记者：“我认为我们只是想赢。”

伊朗军事中央司令部司令阿里·阿卜杜拉希表示，美国正迅速走上导致该地区紧张局势升级的道路。

阿卜杜拉希在伊朗IRIB广播公司发表的评论中表示，地区国家应该明白，美国打算利用其财富、基础设施和资源“作为其薄弱军事力量的防御盾牌”。

他补充说，任何为犯罪和侵略性的美国提供防御盾牌的国家都将被战火吞没。

伊朗周六早些时候对驻有美军的海湾国家科威特发动了无人机袭击，并表示袭击了霍尔木兹海峡的油轮。这条全球重要的能源通道在战斗中已基本关闭。

科威特军方表示，在针对所谓的“伊朗侵略”而启动防空系统数小时后，他们“拦截并摧毁了”进入其领空的敌对无人机。 没有人员伤亡报告。

与此同时，在特朗普总统表示哈马斯和以色列已同意推进停火计划（他称之为和平努力的潜在突破）后不到 48 小时，以色列的袭击在加沙的一家医院造成了一个巨大的弹坑。

特朗普周四宣布，哈马斯已同意“完全解除武装”，以换取以色列撤军。 但一名以色列官员告诉美国有线电视新闻网，在哈马斯首先解除武装之前，以色列不会撤军。

周六对医疗仓库的袭击摧毁了重要的医疗用品，附近数十个帐篷着火，周围的一个流离失所者营地被夷为平地

上周，特朗普在《真相社会》上发誓，每次在霍尔木兹海峡袭击一艘船只，他都会轰炸并摧毁伊朗的一座桥梁或发电厂。

据该地区卫生部称，以色列周六在加沙发动了另一轮袭击，摧毁了阿克萨烈士医院的两个医疗仓库，并损坏了另外两个仓库。

近几个月来，阿克萨烈士医院已成为流离失所的巴勒斯坦人和加沙中部居民的重要生命线，是该地区唯一能够接待大量患者的医疗机构。

该部总干事穆尼尔·阿尔伯什博士在一份声明中表示，“当药品遭到轰炸时，疾病就会成为战争武器。”

这次袭击是在以色列军队发布强制流离失所令几分钟后发生的，袭击摧毁了重要的医疗用品，点燃了附近的数十个帐篷，并夷平了周围的一个流离失所者营地。

视频显示，人们在火山口中寻找医疗用品，包括静脉输液、呼吸管、外科口罩和埋在废墟下的棉球。

阿尔-伯什博士补充说：“在加沙的卫生系统已经遭受 51% 基本药物短缺的情况下，摧毁一个医疗仓库是对医疗保健仅存的最后一条生命线的直接攻击。”

据哥伦比亚广播公司报道，一名美国官员表示，在冲突期间，美国已经在军事和民用方面建立了桥梁。

周五，官员们还权衡了德黑兰全境断电的潜在举措，但没有做出决定。
